steps: Write down the oven settings: 400F, 45 minutes.
Lower the temperature: 400 minus 25 is 375F, and the time stays 45 minutes.
Or shorten the time: 45 × 0.75 = 33.75, rounded to 34 minutes, at the same 400F.

faqs.answer: Either 45 minutes at 375F or check at about 34 minutes at 400F, from a 45 minute oven recipe, but wings often finish sooner. Maker charts give 22 to 26 minutes at 390F for two pounds. Check about a quarter sooner and pull them at 165F.
faqs.question: How long do wings take in the air fryer?

faqs.answer: A tablespoon tossed through two pounds is enough. The skin renders its own fat as it cooks, so wings need less oil than any other chicken part.
faqs.question: Do I need oil on chicken wings?

faqs.answer: No. Sauce burns onto the basket and keeps the skin from crisping. Cook the wings plain, then toss them in warm sauce in a bowl.
faqs.question: Should I sauce wings before air frying?

faqs.answer: A thermometer in the thickest wing, at the bone, reading 165F. The skin should be crisp and golden, and the juices should run clear.
faqs.question: How do I know wings are done?

faqs.answer: Yes, straight from the freezer. Add about 10 minutes to the converted time, shake twice, and check the temperature in two wings before serving.
faqs.question: Can I cook frozen wings in the air fryer?

felicityNote: Dry the wings like you mean it. Paper towels, both sides, no shortcuts. Everything after that is easy.

parts.meaning: The air fryer runs hotter than the dial says, because the fan pushes hot air straight onto the food. Dropping 25F keeps the skin from burning before the meat cooks.
When you lower the temperature, the food still needs the full oven time. The lower heat and the full time balance each other out.
A quarter sooner. Keep the oven temperature and check at three quarters of the oven time. Open the basket then, look, and check the temperature.
The safe internal temperature for chicken, measured in the thickest wing, at the bone.

formula.text: Pick one, never both. Lower the temperature: air fryer temp = oven temp minus 25F, and the time stays the same. Or shorten the time: keep the oven temperature and check at oven time × 0.75. For chicken wings at 400F for 45 minutes: either 375F for 45 minutes, or 400F and check at about 34 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Read the oven settings
howToSteps.text: Find the temperature and time in your recipe. A typical batch of wings bakes at 400F for 45 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Pick one change
howToSteps.text: Pick one change, not both. Either take 25F off the temperature and keep the time, or keep the temperature and check a quarter sooner. 400F for 45 minutes becomes either 375F for 45 minutes or 400F and check at about 34 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Dry and season
howToSteps.text: Pat the wings dry, toss with a tablespoon of oil and seasoning, and load them in a single layer with space between the pieces.

howToSteps.name: Cook, shake, and check
howToSteps.text: Shake the basket twice during the cook. Pull the wings at 165F at the bone.

lede: Wings that bake at 400F for 45 minutes air fry two ways: 375F for the full 45 minutes, or 400F and check at about 34 minutes. Pull them when the thickest part reads 165F and the skin is crisp.

title: Oven to Air Fryer: Chicken Wings
tutorial: Wings are the best argument for an air fryer. In the oven they take 45 minutes at 400F and a wire rack and a sheet pan to clean. In the air fryer the same wings convert two ways: 375F for the full 45 minutes, or 400F and check at about 34 minutes. Either way the skin comes out crisper, because the hot air hits every side.

Dry skin is the whole secret. Pat the wings dry with paper towels before they go in, and toss them with a tablespoon of oil and the seasoning. Wet skin steams. Dry skin crisps. A teaspoon of baking powder in the seasoning mix helps the skin brown, and it is the one trick worth borrowing from the oven recipes.

Wings are the food where the converted time runs longest. The maker charts give 22 to 26 minutes at 390F for two pounds of wings, which is shorter than either option this converter gives from a 45 minute oven recipe. The oven time includes the slow warm-up of a big pan of wings, and the air fryer skips most of that. Trust the shorter time, and trust the thermometer more: 165F at the bone, in the thickest wing.

Do not sauce them before they cook. Sauce goes on after, or in the last five minutes at most. Sauce in the basket burns onto the crisper plate and the wings come out sticky instead of crisp. Toss the cooked wings in the warm sauce in a bowl, the way a wing joint does.

Shake the basket twice, not once. Wings pile up more than any other food, and the ones in the middle stay pale while the ones on top brown. Shake at the halfway mark and again a few minutes later. Two shakes, crisp all over.
